summaries.summary: Generating natural language descriptions of structured data such as tables has grown with sequence to sequence models.
Automatic metrics like BLEU and ROUGE compare generated text to references, but WikiBio references can contain extra information divergent from the table.
The paper proposes PARENT, which uses reference and table union for precision and intersection for recall via an entailment model.
The table-to-text task generates fluent text summarizing records, with evaluation sets of tables, references, generated texts, and n-gram counts.
PARENT evaluates each instance separately by computing precision and recall against both the reference and the table.
A prior extraction model was limited to basketball tables, so the authors train their own model for open-domain WikiBio.
Their pointer-generator network produces linearized tables from text, trained on WikiBio, with extracted tuples compared to ground truth tables.
They define CS, RG, and RG-F metrics from extracted pairs, omitting content ordering because records are not aligned to text.
Experiments compare automatic metrics by Pearson correlation between human scores for models and metric scores on generated outputs.
Main experiments use WikiBio, which is automatically constructed and contains many divergent references, with additional WebNLG results.
Several WikiBio models of varying quality were developed, mainly neural sequence-to-sequence methods plus a template-based baseline.
Models are divided into WikiBio-Systems and WikiBio-Hyperparams, the latter including 13 PG-Net hyperparameter settings.
Human judgments for 16 WikiBio models plus references used paired comparisons aggregated into real-valued scores by Thurstone's method.
Annotation covered 1100 tables, 8800 pairwise comparisons, and around 500 workers, with references scoring lower than PG-Net.
Text-only compared metrics are BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, CIDEr, and CIDEr-D using publicly available implementations.
Information extraction based compared metrics are CS, RG, and RG-F.
Text and table metrics include BLEU-T, PARENT-W, PARENT-C, and tuned PARENT*-W/C variants.
Bootstrap sampling with 500 iterations over 1100 tables estimates correlation variation and reports average correlations.
Bootstrap samples provide a confidence interval for correlation differences between PARENT and other metrics.
Reference-only metrics correlate weakly with humans, often negatively for hyperparams, while BLEU performs best and BLEU-T improves it.
RG-F and both PARENT variants achieve highest correlations, with PARENT-W significantly better than the other two for systems.
Word-overlap entailment outperformed co-occurrence on this dataset, while tuned INLINEFORM0 can yield significantly higher PARENT correlations.
The analysis further examines PARENT-W under different conditions and compares it with other best metrics from Table TABREF37.
Workers labeled whether references were entailed by tables, with 3 independent judgments per pair and majority voting.
PARENT and RG-F remain stable across entailed-example proportions, while BLEU and BLEU-T vary substantially.
Removing entailment probability or Table Recall lowers PARENT-W correlation, showing these components are crucial.
Both PARENT variants significantly outperform other metrics in instance-level pairwise accuracy, though best accuracy is only INLINEFORM0.
WebNLG evaluation uses human ratings for 9 systems on 223 instances describing 1-5 RDF triples with up to 3 references.
Human ratings cover grammaticality, fluency, and semantics, and both PARENT variants are competitive or better on average correlation.
BLEU correlates highest for grammar and fluency, while PARENT does best for semantics and PARENT-C is better among entailment models.
INLINEFORM0 controls recall against table or reference, with WikiBio relying more on the table and WebNLG more on references.
Prior metric studies find no single metric suitable across tasks, and this work first checks divergent table-to-text references.
Divergence is framed as hallucination in the reference text, and PARENT discounts n-grams overlapping neither reference nor table.
PARENT is inspired by iBLEU but rewards source matches, and is a task-specific metric like SARI and Q-BLEU.
PARENT shows highest correlation with humans across divergent WikiBio settings, RG-F is effective, and PARENT is comparable on WebNLG.
Bhuwan Dhingra is supported by Siemens and Google, and the authors thank named colleagues, Sam Wiseman, and reviewers.
The WikiBio information extraction model is a PG-Net with bi-directional LSTMs, attention, copying, and linearized table outputs.
Divergent references cause hallucinated false information, but parsed output tuples can still evaluate generated texts.
Tuned hyperparameters include hidden state size 200, vocabularies of 50000 words, Glove embeddings, Adam, dropout, and beam size 8.
Table TABREF55 shows sample references and corresponding predictions from the best performing WikiBio model, PG-Net.
